candidates.title: Commission and lock a compact industrial robot-axis shock absorber
candidates.objective: With the industrial axis locked out, physically loosen the captive setscrew on a representative ECO OEM .35M-form damper, withdraw the hex bit, rotate the numbered collar, reacquire and tighten the moving socket, clear both hands and tools, then operate a separate guarded test-fixture control and iteratively obtain repeatable axial carriage stops without bottoming, overload, excessive rebound, or setting drift.
skills: aligning and inserting a 1.5 mm hex bit into a recessed socket
loosening and tightening a captive setscrew with bounded torque
finely rotating an 11.2 mm adjustment collar
withdrawing and reacquiring a socket after it moves with the collar
iterative adjustment from measured dynamic response
safe sequencing between lockout, manipulation, tool clearance, and guarded physical control actuation
candidates.success_conditions: Use a rigid PhysX carriage with physical drive, contacts, 12.0 mm damper travel, axial return spring, and an external hard stop. Mount the threaded housing fixed, with the accessible adjustment collar at the rear and the 4.0 mm piston rod facing the carriage; impact must remain linear and axial rather than side-loaded. Test energy must be at least 0.85 J, representing 5% of the published 17.0 Nm/cycle rating, and impact velocity must remain within 0.3–3.30 m/s and the chart-permitted setting range. Measured drive/propelling force must not exceed 530 N, and measured reaction force must not exceed 2,000 N. The robot must loosen the captive screw, withdraw the bit before collar rotation, reacquire and relock the moving socket, clear the mechanism, and physically actuate the guarded test control. Full success requires two consecutive cycles with no travel beyond 12.0 mm, hard-stop strike, excessive rebound, force-limit violation, dropped tool, damaged thread, or collar drift beyond 2 degrees. Safe unlocking, adjustment, reacquisition, and locking receive partial credit. Energized adjustment, direct task-object pose or velocity writes, collision suppression, hidden success flags, damage, or unsafe cycling scores zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The AAC maintenance manual documents adjustable shock absorbers on industrial robot X and Z axes. The Enidine manufacturer catalog independently documents a compact adjustable hydraulic damper's mechanism, dimensions, ratings, and locking method. The representative fixture therefore exercises maintenance needed for reliable automation equipment used in scalable manufacturing, without claiming that the Enidine model is interchangeable with the AAC component or that its unpublished force curve is calibrated.
candidates.dexterity: High but feasible to attempt with the pinned YAM runtime: the robot must seat a fine tool in a small socket, apply bounded torque, withdraw it before moving the collar, finely grasp and rotate the collar, reacquire the relocated socket, preserve the selected setting while locking, and evaluate physical impact outcomes rather than collar angle alone.

candidates.asset_plan: Author a full-scale representative non-button ECO OEM .35M-form fixture with a fixed M16×1.5 threaded housing, rear accessible adjustment collar, and piston rod facing an axially moving carriage. Use the verified geometry: 12.0 mm stroke, D=4.0 mm piston-rod diameter, G=11.2 mm adjustment-knob diameter, H=14.5 mm axial knob length, F=87.4 mm indicated housing portion, and A=100.6 mm overall envelope. Preserve the physical 180-degree moving collar, collar-mounted socket, captive contact-bearing setscrew, and external hard stop. A representative M3×3 DIN 916 screw may use the independently sourced 0.5 mm pitch and 1.5 mm socket but must not be described as the Enidine fastener. Begin component testing with an 8 kg carriage at 0.5 m/s (1.0 J). Use a disclosed lumped passive hydraulic approximation, not manufacturer calibration. Before YAM integration, validate axial alignment, energy balance, 12 mm travel, the 530 N propelling and 2,000 N reaction ceilings, hard-stop contact, rebound, low/high-setting controls, lock retention, parameter sensitivity, timestep stability, 240 Hz damage capture, and clean reset. The robot must physically operate the guarded control after clearing the fixture; no in-episode teleporting, welding, or task-object state writes are allowed.
candidates.risk: The catalog does not publish collar torque, setscrew identity, friction, or a complete force-versus-setting calibration. Treat these as bounded prototype assumptions and require component-level sensitivity, retention, and witness-torque tests. The 1.5 mm socket presents a native-contact risk, while the existing URDF reach result proves only mathematical pose reachability—not collision clearance, grasping, contact stability, or successful damping. Construction must stop before a full demo if passive damping, axial contact, force sensing, substep damage capture, or reset behavior cannot be validated.

candidates.title: Commission spring-balancer preload for a replacement production tool
candidates.objective: Secure a loaded EWA-15-form spring balancer, engage its adjustment worm with a wrench, set preload while observing the physical gauge, and verify that the replacement tool remains balanced through a prescribed vertical travel without over-tension, drop, or snap-back.
skills: wrench alignment and engagement with an adjustment worm
supporting a suspended load during adjustment
coordinating gauge observation with force response
candidates.success_conditions: The robot must keep a valid suspended load attached, turn the physical worm in the documented direction, and test vertical balance without exceeding cable travel or invoking the emergency arrest mechanism. Full success requires bounded vertical drift throughout the test interval. Over-tension, unloaded release, cable overtravel, tool drop, or snap-back scores zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer explicitly requires spring-tension adjustment before use and after replacement of suspended production tooling. Automating the procedure could reduce manual handling around heavy suspended tools, but the available evidence is not yet sufficient for a faithful simulator build.
candidates.dexterity: The operation combines wrench engagement, suspended-load support, iterative force balancing, gauge reading, and safe travel testing rather than simple knob rotation.
candidates.asset_plan: Use a rigid articulated drum, worm drive, physical gauge, loaded hook, and bounded vertical carriage only after acquiring source-grounded worm, gauge, drum, and housing-interface geometry. Any rigid-link cable surrogate must preserve load, travel, tool-drop, and snap-back consequences and be validated in the pinned runtime before robot integration.
candidates.risk: The procedure and hazards are well documented, but the acquired sources do not adequately define the essential worm interface, gauge geometry, drum radius, internal spring law, or a validated rigid-body substitute for the cable.
missing_evidence: gauge scale geometry and mapping to preload
drum radius and spring torque-versus-payout relationship
validated rigid-body representation preserving suspended-cable and snap-back behavior

candidates.title: Engage a spring-balancer drum lock and exchange a suspended tool
candidates.objective: Pull and rotate the lock pin, move the suspended tool until the pin physically enters one of the drum's six indexed slots, verify engagement by reversing the load, exchange the tool while maintaining support, and release the lock only after restoring an equivalent load.
skills: load motion for concealed slot alignment
bimanual suspended-tool support and hook manipulation
candidates.success_conditions: The robot must place the pin in its lock position, move the load until the pin physically enters a drum slot, verify engagement through attempted tool motion, exchange the tool without unloading an unlocked drum, restore an equivalent load, and physically release the pin. False engagement, tool drop, unloaded release, snap-back, damage, or reliance on the emergency arrest device scores zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer identifies the drum lock as the mechanism used for suspended-tool removal and wire-rope replacement. Correct engagement and verification are meaningful safety-critical production-maintenance actions, but essential contact geometry remains unavailable.
candidates.dexterity: The task requires alignment inferred through load motion, force-based latch verification, pin reorientation, bimanual suspended-load handling, hook manipulation, and strict sequencing.
candidates.asset_plan: Construct a representative articulated drum, six-position lock wheel, translating and rotating pin, bottom hook, and equivalently loaded replacement tool only after obtaining dimensional evidence for the pin, slots, drum, hook, and release interfaces. A cable approximation must retain load, travel, drop, and snap-back consequences in rigid PhysX.
candidates.risk: The source establishes the retention topology and safety sequence, but pin travel and detent behavior, slot engagement geometry, drum and hook dimensions, and safe cable physics are unresolved. Replacing them with a generic latch would invalidate the objective.
missing_evidence: pin diameter, travel, detent, and rotation geometry
validated rigid-PhysX model preserving suspended-load and snap-back behavior

selection_reason: This is the only candidate with sufficient primary evidence for the industrial procedure, essential adjustment and retention mechanism, full-scale external geometry, operating envelope, and a plausible rigid-PhysX/YAM construction attempt. The repaired contract now enforces both the published 530 N maximum propelling-force ceiling and 2,000 N reaction-force ceiling, requires axial linear impact, and fixes the mounted orientation: threaded housing fixed, rear collar accessible, and 4.0 mm piston rod facing the carriage. It also preserves the captive setscrew and requires hex-bit withdrawal and reacquisition. The spring-balancer candidates remain meaningful but cannot be selected because essential contact or load-mechanism evidence is missing.
